concepts.name: Main asset classes
concepts.summary: Name and describe stocks, bonds and cash equivalents and how each makes money for an owner.

concepts.name: Risk and return trade-off
concepts.summary: Explain why higher expected returns generally come with greater uncertainty and possible losses.

concepts.name: Investment funds
concepts.summary: Explain that a fund pools many investors' money to hold a basket of assets, and distinguish index funds from actively managed funds.

concepts.name: Saving versus investing
concepts.summary: Distinguish keeping money safe for near-term needs from investing it for long-term goals, and explain inflation's role.

concepts.name: Compound growth
concepts.summary: Understand how returns earn further returns over time and why starting early matters.

concepts.name: Investment time horizon
concepts.summary: Define time horizon as the time until money is needed and recall that it shapes which investments suit a goal.

misconceptions.text: Investing is the same as gambling or picking winning stocks.
Money in a savings account is risk-free in every sense, so it is the best place for long-term money.
You need a large sum of money to start investing.

concepts.name: Diversification
concepts.summary: Apply the idea of spreading money across many assets so one failure does not sink the portfolio.

concepts.name: Fund fees and expense ratios
concepts.summary: Calculate how annual fees reduce returns over decades and compare the cost of funds.

concepts.name: Asset allocation
concepts.summary: Choose a split between stocks, bonds and cash that fits a goal and time horizon.

concepts.name: Investment accounts and tax wrappers
concepts.summary: Explain the purpose of general brokerage and tax-advantaged accounts and choose an appropriate one for a goal.

concepts.name: Market volatility and drawdowns
concepts.summary: Understand that prices fluctuate, that declines are normal, and that markets have historically recovered over long periods.

concepts.name: Regular contributions and dollar-cost averaging
concepts.summary: Set up automatic recurring investments and explain how they spread out purchase prices.

concepts.name: Bond basics: yield and maturity
concepts.summary: Describe coupons, maturity and credit quality, and why bond prices fall when interest rates rise.

misconceptions.text: Owning many different funds always means a portfolio is well diversified.
A fee of 1 percent a year is trivial and does not matter much.
Bonds are completely safe and cannot lose value.

concepts.name: Risk tolerance versus risk capacity
aliases: willingness vs ability to take risk
concepts.summary: Distinguish emotional comfort with losses from financial ability to absorb them, and use both to set allocation.

concepts.name: Return decomposition and real returns
concepts.summary: Break returns into price change and income, and adjust for inflation and fees to judge actual growth.

concepts.name: Tax-efficient asset location
concepts.summary: Analyse which holdings suit taxable versus tax-advantaged accounts to reduce tax drag.

concepts.name: Correlation and diversification benefit
concepts.summary: Analyse how assets that do not move together reduce portfolio volatility, and when correlations rise.

concepts.name: Portfolio construction from goals
concepts.summary: Design a simple diversified portfolio of low-cost funds matched to specific goals, horizons and risk tolerance.

concepts.name: Behavioural biases in investing
concepts.summary: Identify loss aversion, herding, overconfidence and recency bias in one's own decisions and set rules to counter them.

concepts.name: Rebalancing strategies
concepts.summary: Restore target weights using calendar or threshold rules and new contributions, accounting for costs and taxes.

misconceptions.text: Risk tolerance is only how you feel about losses, so your financial situation does not matter.
Rebalancing is meant to boost returns rather than control risk.
Last year's best-performing fund is the best choice going forward.

concepts.name: Evaluating active versus passive
concepts.summary: Judge the evidence on active manager performance after fees and decide when active strategies might be justified.

concepts.name: Factor and style exposures
concepts.summary: Analyse a portfolio's tilts toward factors such as value, size or quality and what they imply for risk and returns.

concepts.name: Risk-adjusted performance measures
concepts.summary: Use Sharpe ratio, standard deviation and maximum drawdown to compare investments and portfolios critically.

concepts.name: Valuation and expected returns
concepts.summary: Evaluate how starting valuations and risk premiums inform realistic long-run return assumptions.

concepts.name: Sequence-of-returns risk and withdrawals
concepts.summary: Evaluate withdrawal strategies and how the order of returns affects portfolio longevity in retirement.

concepts.name: Bond duration and credit risk
concepts.summary: Analyse how duration, credit quality and inflation affect bond fund behaviour and its role in a portfolio.

concepts.name: Glide paths and lifecycle allocation
concepts.summary: Assess how allocation should shift over a lifetime given human capital, goals and target-date fund designs.

misconceptions.text: A higher Sharpe ratio or past return proves a manager has skill rather than luck.
Factor premiums are guaranteed to pay off over any reasonable period.
A safe withdrawal rate based on average returns will work regardless of when you retire.

concepts.name: Critiquing portfolio theory assumptions
concepts.summary: Evaluate the assumptions and limits of mean-variance optimisation and efficient markets, including fat tails and regime change.

concepts.name: Designing an investment policy
concepts.summary: Create a complete policy covering allocation, rebalancing, tax, withdrawal and behavioural rules tailored to a client's circumstances.

concepts.name: Total-wealth and liability-driven planning
concepts.summary: Construct portfolios that integrate human capital, housing, pensions and future liabilities with matching assets.

concepts.name: Assessing alternatives and complex products
concepts.summary: Judge the costs, risks, liquidity and complexity of products such as leveraged funds, private assets and crypto before including any.

concepts.name: Stress testing and tail risk
concepts.summary: Evaluate a portfolio's resilience using historical scenarios and simulations and recognise their model limits.

concepts.name: Advice quality and conflicts of interest
concepts.summary: Evaluate advice, products and marketing for incentives, hidden costs and evidence quality.

concepts.name: Adapting strategy to regime shifts
concepts.summary: Develop principled responses to shifts in inflation, rates or market structure without abandoning a disciplined plan.

misconceptions.text: Sophisticated optimisation or complex products reliably beat a simple diversified portfolio.
Monte Carlo or backtest results give accurate probabilities of future outcomes.
Changing strategy to match each macro forecast is a sign of expertise rather than risk.
